front: What is ARN (Amazon Resource Name) in one sentence?
back: Universal resource identifier for IAM policies, CloudTrail, cross-service references, and CLI --resource-arn. Format is strict — one wrong segment = AccessDenied or wrong resource.

front: Explain the mental model of ARN (Amazon Resource Name) (how the system thinks).
back: Every AWS resource that policies reference gets an ARN: partition, service, region (sometimes empty), account, resource path. IAM evaluates string match on ARNs in policies; typos and missing account ids are silent until runtime.

front: Which standard commands / workflow do you use for ARN (Amazon Resource Name)?
back: arn : partition : service : region : account-id : resource

front: Given a broken ARN (Amazon Resource Name) setup, what is your first validation command?
back: arn : partition : service : region : account-id : resource

front: What are the production-safe defaults for ARN (Amazon Resource Name)?
back: aws — commercial; aws-us-gov, aws-cn — isolated partitions; ARNs don't cross partitions.

front: Symptom: Policy "looks right" but Deny — what do you check and fix?
back: Check: Wrong account id in ARN · Fix: Copy ARN from describe-* API

front: Symptom: Cross-region copy/snapshot fail — what do you check and fix?
back: Check: Source/dest ARNs region mismatch · Fix: Use region-local ARNs

front: Symptom: KMS InvalidArnException — what do you check and fix?
back: Check: Key ARN vs alias (alias/xxx) · Fix: Use key id ARN in key policies

front: Symptom: EventBridge target fail — what do you check and fix?
back: Check: Target ARN service mismatch · Fix: Verify full target ARN format

front: Symptom: Organization SCP not applying — what do you check and fix?
back: Check: ARN in member account vs org id · Fix: SCP uses different principal patterns

front: Gotcha with ARN (Amazon Resource Name): what silently fails?
back: S3 ARN has no region in resource — but bucket is regional; policies still work; some services need bucket location for cross-region ops.

front: When should you NOT use ARN (Amazon Resource Name)?
back: Human-readable naming in automation — construct from API responses; don't hand-build instance ids. ARN as secret — ARNs are identifiers, not authorization; knowing ARN doesn't grant access without policy.

front: What is AWS EBS (Elastic Block Store) in one sentence?
back: Network-attached block volumes for EC2 — persistent disk, snapshots, resize, and Delete on Termination gotcha.

front: Explain the mental model of AWS EBS (Elastic Block Store) (how the system thinks).
back: EBS volumes are AZ-scoped block devices attached to EC2 as /dev/xvdf etc. OS sees raw disk — format, mount, persist data independent of instance lifecycle unless volume is deleted on instance terminate. Snapshots → S3-backed incremental backups → new volume in any AZ (copy region for DR).

front: Which standard commands / workflow do you use for AWS EBS (Elastic Block Store)?
back: EC2 instance ← attach → EBS volume (gp3/io2) → AMI / DR / clone → aws ec2 create-volume --availability-zone us-east-1a --size 100 --volume-type gp3 → aws ec2 attach-volume --volume-id vol-xxx --instance-id i-xxx --device /dev/sdf → aws ec2 create-snapshot --volume-id vol-xxx --description "pre-migration"

front: Given a broken AWS EBS (Elastic Block Store) setup, what is your first validation command?
back: EC2 instance ← attach → EBS volume (gp3/io2)

front: What are the production-safe defaults for AWS EBS (Elastic Block Store)?
back: Launch template / instance Block device mapping → Delete on termination Uncheck for data volumes you must keep when replacing instance

front: Symptom: Data gone after terminate — what do you check and fix?
back: Check: Delete on termination = true · Fix: Restore from snapshot; fix mapping before next terminate

front: Symptom: Volume won't attach — what do you check and fix?
back: Check: AZ mismatch · Fix: Volume and instance same AZ (or detach/move)

front: Symptom: Full disk — what do you check and fix?
back: Check: df -h · Fix: Extend volume + filesystem; don't just restart

front: Symptom: Poor IOPS — what do you check and fix?
back: Check: CloudWatch VolumeQueueLength · Fix: gp3 provisioned IOPS; io2 for sustained

front: Symptom: Snapshot slow first time — what do you check and fix?
back: Check: Normal · Fix: Incremental snapshots faster after

front: Symptom: Corrupt FS after crash — what do you check and fix?
back: Check: fsck · Fix: Restore snapshot; enable fsync app-side

front: Gotcha with AWS EBS (Elastic Block Store): what silently fails?
back: Root volume default delete on terminate — usually desired; data volume must opt out explicitly. EBS ≠ backup strategy — snapshots need lifecycle; test restore. Encryption — enable default EBS encryption per account/region for compliance.

front: When should you NOT use AWS EBS (Elastic Block Store)?
back: Don't use EBS for shared POSIX across many EC2 — use EFS or S3. Don't attach same volume to two instances simultaneously (except cluster FS products).

front: What is AWS EC2 in one sentence?
back: Virtual machines in a VPC — pick AMI, instance type, subnet/SG, and know what still bills after terminate. AWS EC2 User Guide + finance surprises from orphaned EIPs/NAT.

front: Explain the mental model of AWS EC2 (how the system thinks).
back: An EC2 instance is compute on shared hardware (or Dedicated Host) with ENI(s) in a subnet. Launch = AMI + instance type + key pair/instance profile + Security group. Storage = root + optional EBS (Elastic Block Store) volumes. Terminate ≠ delete all billable artifacts.

front: Which standard commands / workflow do you use for AWS EC2?
back: Launch template ──► AMI + type + subnet + SG + user-data → aws ec2 describe-instances --filters "Name=tag:Env,Values=prod" \ → aws ec2 terminate-instances --instance-ids i-xxx → aws ec2 describe-volumes --filters "Name=status,Values=available" → aws ec2 describe-addresses --query 'Addresses[?AssociationId==null]'

front: Given a broken AWS EC2 setup, what is your first validation command?
back: Launch template ──► AMI + type + subnet + SG + user-data

front: What are the production-safe defaults for AWS EC2?
back: Check subnet AZ matches resilience plan — describe-instances → Placement.AvailabilityZone. Multi-AZ ASG: one subnet per AZ in LT/ASG.

front: Symptom: Instance unreachable (SSH/app) — what do you check and fix?
back: Check: SG, NACL, route, public IP/subnet · Fix: Full path debug (AWS Networking, Security group)

front: Symptom: Status checks failed — what do you check and fix?
back: Check: System vs instance check in console · Fix: Reboot; migrate if hardware; fix disk full (instance check)

front: Symptom: Out of CPU credits (T-family) — what do you check and fix?
back: Check: CloudWatch CPUCreditBalance · Fix: Unlimited mode or resize to M/C family

front: Symptom: User-data didn't run — what do you check and fix?
back: Check: /var/log/cloud-init-output.log; MIME multipart · Fix: Fix script; re-run with cloud-init clean

front: Symptom: IAM role calls fail on instance — what do you check and fix?
back: Check: Profile attached? IMDS reachable? · Fix: Attach profile; curl IMDSv2 token flow

front: Symptom: Bill after terminate — what do you check and fix?
back: Check: EBS volumes, EIP, NAT GW, snapshots · Fix: Delete orphans (see WARNING below)

front: Symptom: Wrong region/AZ capacity — what do you check and fix?
back: Check: InsufficientInstanceCapacity · Fix: Retry another AZ/type; use capacity reservations

front: Gotcha with AWS EC2: what silently fails?
back: Terminate EC2, then manually delete EBS volumes, Elastic IPs, and NAT gateways — terminate stops compute; EBS/EIP/NAT keep charging if left behind.

front: When should you NOT use AWS EC2?
back: Long-running stateless web at scale without ASG — use Auto Scaling Group + ALB. Batch/analytics — consider Fargate, AWS Lambda, or Spot Fleet for cost. Bare metal driver/hardware timing needs — consider Dedicated Hosts or on-prem.

front: What is AWS ECR in one sentence?
back: Private Docker registry in AWS — store images per region/account; IAM controls push/pull; integrates with ECS/EKS/Lambda/EC2. Not Docker Hub; not interchangeable without auth + URL change.

front: Explain the mental model of AWS ECR (how the system thinks).
back: ECR holds repositories of image manifests + layers (OCI-compatible). Each region has its own registry endpoint: {account}.dkr.ecr.{region}.amazonaws.com. Pull/push uses IAM (or bot IAM user in legacy setups) + short-lived authorization token from ecr:GetAuthorizationToken.

front: Which standard commands / workflow do you use for AWS ECR?
back: docker push ──► ECR API (auth token) ──► layer upload ──► repository:tag → ECS/EKS/Lambda ◄── pull (execution role iam: ecr:* on repo ARN) → AWS_REGION=us-east-1 → ACCOUNT=123456789012 → REPO=my-app

front: Given a broken AWS ECR setup, what is your first validation command?
back: docker push ──► ECR API (auth token) ──► layer upload ──► repository:tag

front: What are the production-safe defaults for AWS ECR?
back: ecr:BatchGetImage, ecr:GetDownloadUrlForLayer on repo ARN. Same region pull avoids cross-region data charge; replicate for multi-region DR.

front: Symptom: no basic auth credentials on push — what do you check and fix?
back: Check: aws ecr get-login-password; IAM · Fix: Login; CI role GetAuthorizationToken

front: Symptom: denied: repository does not exist — what do you check and fix?
back: Check: Repo name/region/account in URL · Fix: Create repo; fix URI

front: Symptom: ECS/EKS CannotPullContainerError — what do you check and fix?
back: Check: Execution role ECR perms; repo policy · Fix: Add ECR pull actions; private repo policy if cross-account

front: Symptom: Pull works locally, fails in cluster — what do you check and fix?
back: Check: Cluster in private subnet without NAT/endpoint · Fix: ECR VPC endpoints

front: Symptom: Image scan shows CVEs — what do you check and fix?
back: Check: Base image stale · Fix: Rebuild from patched base; block deploy on CRITICAL (policy)

front: Symptom: Storage cost creep — what do you check and fix?
back: Check: Untagged manifests · Fix: Lifecycle policy; delete old tags

front: Gotcha with AWS ECR: what silently fails?
back: Auth token expires in 12 hours — CI must login each job (or use credential helper).

front: When should you NOT use AWS ECR?
back: Public OSS images — Docker Hub / ghcr.io unless mirroring into ECR for rate-limit/air-gap. Large binary blobs unrelated to containers — S3, not ECR. Single tiny Lambda zip deploy — container overhead may not pay off.

front: What is AWS Lambda in one sentence?
back: Event-driven compute that runs your handler, then stops billing — configure memory/timeout/role correctly or you pay for cold starts, timeouts, and over-privileged roles. AWS Lambda Developer Guide + production bills from retry storms.

front: For --timeout in AWS Lambda, what is the key fact?
back: 3–30s for APIs; longer for batch — Fail fast; don't hide hung deps

front: For --memory-size in AWS Lambda, what is the key fact?
back: Start 256–512; load-test — Under-memory = CPU starve + timeouts

front: For --architectures in AWS Lambda, what is the key fact?
back: arm64 when deps allow — Often cheaper/faster per GB-s

front: For Env vars in AWS Lambda, what is the key fact?
back: Non-secrets only — Secrets → Secrets Manager / SSM, not plain env

front: For Ephemeral /tmp in AWS Lambda, what is the key fact?
back: ≤ 512 MB–10 GB (config) — Not durable storage

front: Explain the mental model of AWS Lambda (how the system thinks).
back: Lambda is stateless compute on demand: an event (API Gateway, SQS, S3, EventBridge, cron) invokes a handler in a managed runtime (or container image). You do not manage servers; you manage execution role, memory, timeout, concurrency, and triggers. Cold start = new execution environment; warm reuse is best-effort, not a guarantee.

front: Which standard commands / workflow do you use for AWS Lambda?
back: Event source ──► Lambda service ──► execution env (runtime + your code) → aws configure # or: aws sso login → aws sts get-caller-identity → Attach least-privilege policies. Minimum for logs: → VPC-attached functions also need:

back: Event source ──► Lambda service ──► execution env (runtime + your code)

front: What are the production-safe defaults for AWS Lambda?
back: Need: account access, a region, and an IAM role Lambda can assume (lambda.amazonaws.com trust).

front: Symptom: AccessDeniedException / can't talk to S3/Dynamo — what do you check and fix?
back: Check: Execution role policies; resource policies · Fix: Least-privilege allow on role; fix resource ARN (ARN (Amazon Resource Name))

front: Symptom: Timeout near limit — what do you check and fix?
back: Check: CW Logs duration; downstream latency; memory · Fix: Raise memory (CPU) or timeout; fix hung I/O; shorten work

front: Symptom: Cold start latency spikes — what do you check and fix?
back: Check: Init duration in logs; VPC?; large package · Fix: Slim package; arm64; provisioned concurrency; avoid VPC if possible

front: Symptom: ResourceConflictException on update — what do you check and fix?
back: Check: Previous update still in progress · Fix: Poll LastUpdateStatus; serialize deploys

front: Symptom: Throttling (429 / Rate exceeded) — what do you check and fix?
back: Check: Reserved concurrency too low; account concurrency · Fix: Raise reserved or account limit; backpressure at source

front: Symptom: Async retries / duplicate side effects — what do you check and fix?
back: Check: Event source retry + DLQ empty · Fix: Idempotent handler; DLQ + alarm; SQS partial batch failure

front: Symptom: Can't reach RDS in VPC — what do you check and fix?
back: Check: Subnets, SG, route, ENI role policy · Fix: Fix SG path; attach VPCAccessExecutionRole; multi-AZ subnets

front: Symptom: CodeStorageExceededException — what do you check and fix?
back: Check: Account code storage quota · Fix: Delete old versions; use images or S3 for large artifacts

front: Symptom: Handler not found — what do you check and fix?
back: Check: --handler path vs export name · Fix: Fix file.export; zip from correct root (no nested junk folder)

front: Gotcha with AWS Lambda: what silently fails?
back: Retries are a feature — SQS, async invoke, and stream consumers retry. Non-idempotent writes → duplicate charges, double emails, double orders. Design for at-least-once.

front: When should you NOT use AWS Lambda?
back: Steady 24/7 high-QPS with tiny payloads — often cheaper/simpler on ECS/Fargate or EC2 behind an ALB once always-on. Workloads needing >15 minutes wall clock — Step Functions + workers, Batch, or a job runner. WebSockets / sticky long-lived connections — API Gateway WebSocket + Lambda is possible but awkward; consider dedicated connection brokers. Heavy GPU / specialized hardware —…

front: What is AWS Networking in one sentence?
back: VPC + subnets + routing + SG/NACL — the network shell every AWS service lives in. AWS Well-Architected (Reliability/Security) + on-call VPC debug muscle memory.

front: What is CIDR?
back: /16 VPC, /24 subnets — leave headroom; overlapping CIDR blocks cannot be peered later.

front: What is Multi-AZ?
back: always span ≥2 AZs for anything that matters; single-AZ NAT is a known SPOF (accept cost or run NAT per AZ).

front: What is DNS?
back: enable enableDnsHostnames + enableDnsSupport on VPC (required for private hosted zones and many managed services).

front: Explain the mental model of AWS Networking (how the system thinks).
back: AWS networking is regional isolation inside a VPC: you own private IP space, carve subnets per AZ, attach route tables (where traffic goes), and gate traffic with Security Groups (stateful, instance-level) and NACLs (stateless, subnet-level). Public subnets reach the internet via Internet Gateway (IGW); private subnets reach out via NAT Gateway/GW or VPC endpoints (stay on AWS backbon…

front: Which standard commands / workflow do you use for AWS Networking?
back: Internet ──► IGW ──► public subnet (ALB, bastion) → aws ec2 describe-instances --instance-ids i-xxx \ → aws ec2 describe-route-tables --filters "Name=association.subnet-id,Values=subnet-xxx" → aws ec2 create-network-insights-path --source i-xxx --destination i-yyy --protocol tcp --destination-port 443

front: Given a broken AWS Networking setup, what is your first validation command?
back: Internet ──► IGW ──► public subnet (ALB, bastion)

front: What are the production-safe defaults for AWS Networking?
back: CIDR: /16 VPC, /24 subnets — leave headroom; overlapping CIDR blocks cannot be peered later. Multi-AZ: always span ≥2 AZs for anything that matters; single-AZ NAT is a known SPOF (accept cost or run NAT per AZ). DNS: enable enableDnsHostnames + enableDnsSupport on VPC (required for private hosted zones and many managed services).

front: Symptom: EC2 has no public IP but "should" — what do you check and fix?
back: Check: Subnet auto-assign public IP; IGW attached to VPC · Fix: Enable auto-assign or attach EIP; verify public subnet route to IGW

front: Symptom: Private instance can't reach internet — what do you check and fix?
back: Check: NAT GW in public subnet? Route 0.0.0.0/0 → NAT on private RT? · Fix: Fix route table association; NAT GW must sit in public subnet with IGW route

front: Symptom: Works instance-to-instance in same SG, fails cross-SG — what do you check and fix?
back: Check: Security group inbound/outbound rules · Fix: Add SG-to-SG rule (reference SG id, not CIDR) on both sides if needed

front: Symptom: RDS/Redis "connection timed out" from app — what do you check and fix?
back: Check: App in private subnet? SG allows app SG on DB port? NACL 1024-65535 return? · Fix: Open SG; verify NACL ephemeral return (NACL is stateless)

front: Symptom: DNS resolves wrong / not at all — what do you check and fix?
back: Check: VPC DNS settings; Route53 resolver rules; hybrid DNS · Fix: Enable DNS on VPC; check PHZ association; forwarders for on-prem

front: Symptom: Peering/Transit Gateway "partial" connectivity — what do you check and fix?
back: Check: Route tables on both sides; SG still independent · Fix: Add routes both directions; SG rules don't inherit from peering

front: Symptom: NAT GW bill spike — what do you check and fix?
back: Check: CloudWatch BytesOutToDestination; which AZ/subnet? · Fix: VPC endpoints for S3/ECR; fix hairpin traffic; review scrapers

front: Gotcha with AWS Networking: what silently fails?
back: Security Groups are stateful; NACLs are stateless. SG "allow 443 in" implies return traffic. NACL needs explicit ephemeral port range outbound and inbound for return packets — classic "SG looks fine, still broken" cause.

front: When should you NOT use AWS Networking?
back: Default VPC for production — no blast-radius separation, CIDR collisions when peering. Public IPs on app/database tiers — use ALB + private subnets; bastion or SSM Session Manager for admin. NACL micromanagement — start with SG-only; add NACLs for explicit deny (compliance) or subnet-level guardrails. One NAT GW for multi-AZ prod HA — AZ failure kills all private egress.

front: What is EBS (Elastic Block Store)?
back: EBS in AWS stands for Elastic Block Store. Purpose: It provides persistent block storage for EC2 instances. Use: It stores data such as file systems, databases, or application data. Scalability: EBS volumes can be dynamically resized, and you can attach them …

front: What is Purpose?
back: It provides persistent block storage for EC2 instances.

front: What is Use?
back: It stores data such as file systems, databases, or application data.

front: What is Scalability?
back: EBS volumes can be dynamically resized, and you can attach them to EC2 instances.

front: What is Types?

front: What is AWS Elastic IP (EIP) in one sentence?
back: Static public IPv4 in a region — survives stop/start, anchors DNS A records, and fronts NAT gateways. AWS EC2 User Guide (Elastic IP addresses) + billing surprises from orphaned or stopped-instance EIPs.

front: Explain the mental model of AWS Elastic IP (EIP) (how the system thinks).
back: An Elastic IP is a regional, static public IPv4 you allocate into your account and associate with a network interface (usually an EC2 instance's primary ENI, or a NAT Gateway's ENI). It is not tied to an AZ until associated — the ENI's subnet/AZ defines placement.

back: See How to connect Godaddy domain with AWS EC2 instance for full registrar + HTTPS runbook.

front: Symptom: Can't SSH/curl by EIP — what do you check and fix?
back: Check: Security group inbound; app bind address; NACL · Fix: Open 22/80/443; listen 0.0.0.0; verify subnet is public + IGW route

front: Symptom: EIP shows associated but no inbound — what do you check and fix?
back: Check: Route table on instance subnet → IGW? · Fix: Associate subnet with public route table; attach IGW to VPC

front: Symptom: DNS points to old IP after change — what do you check and fix?
back: Check: dig +short domain A; TTL cache · Fix: Lower TTL before migration; update A/ALIAS to new EIP

front: Symptom: IP changed after stop/start — what do you check and fix?
back: Check: Was auto public IP, not EIP · Fix: Allocate + associate EIP before relying on DNS

front: Symptom: AddressLimitExceeded — what do you check and fix?
back: Check: describe-addresses count in region · Fix: Release unused EIPs; request quota increase

front: Symptom: EIP won't associate to ENI — what do you check and fix?
back: Check: ENI in public subnet? Same region? · Fix: Move ENI to public subnet or pick ENI in correct VPC/region

front: Symptom: Private instance "has EIP" but no internet in — what do you check and fix?
back: Check: Expectation mismatch — inbound only via EIP path · Fix: Outbound from private subnet needs NAT, not EIP on instance

front: Symptom: Bill for "EC2-Other" / Elastic IP — what do you check and fix?
back: Check: EIP unassociated or on stopped instance · Fix: Start instance, disassociate + release, or associate to running resource

front: Symptom: NAT works one AZ, not another — what do you check and fix?
back: Check: Per-AZ NAT + route table association · Fix: Each private subnet RT must point to NAT in same AZ

front: Symptom: Association fails after ENI swap — what do you check and fix?
back: Check: Stale association on old ENI · Fix: Disassociate from old ENI; associate to new primary ENI

front: Gotcha with AWS Elastic IP (EIP): what silently fails?
back: Unassociated EIP bills hourly — and EIPs on stopped instances also bill. Free tier: first one EIP associated with a running instance is free; extras and idle EIPs are not.

front: When should you NOT use AWS Elastic IP (EIP)?
back: Production web behind scaling or blue/green — use ALB/NLB + Route53 ALIAS; don't pin users to one instance EIP. Private app/database tiers — no public IP; use internal LB and NAT (Network Address Translation) for outbound only. IPv6-only workloads — use IPv6 addressing; EIP is IPv4-only. Avoiding NAT cost by EIP on every instance — security and ops overhead; prefer VPC endpoin…

front: What is IAM in one sentence?
back: Who can do what to which resource — users, groups, roles, policies, permission boundaries, and SCPs (org level). AWS IAM best practices + audit findings from over-privileged CI roles.

front: Explain the mental model of IAM (how the system thinks).
back: IAM is AWS's authorization graph: principals (users, roles, federated identities) assume policies (identity-based + resource-based) evaluated at API call time. Roles (with aws STS (Security Token Service)) are the production default; users + access keys are legacy/break-glass.

front: Which standard commands / workflow do you use for IAM?
back: Request ──► AuthN (who) ──► IAM policy eval ──► Allow/Deny ──► API → Attach managed or inline policy with least privilege — e.g. s3:GetObject on arn:aws:s3:::my-bucket/*, not s3:*.

front: Given a broken IAM setup, what is your first validation command?
back: Request ──► AuthN (who) ──► IAM policy eval ──► Allow/Deny ──► API

front: What are the production-safe defaults for IAM?
back: Attach managed or inline policy with least privilege — e.g. s3:GetObject on arn:aws:s3:::my-bucket/*, not s3:*.

front: Symptom: AccessDenied despite "Admin" — what do you check and fix?
back: Check: SCP? Permission boundary? Session policy? · Fix: Org SCP; boundary; explicit Deny in policy

front: Symptom: CI deploy role stopped working — what do you check and fix?
back: Check: OIDC trust repo branch; role session name · Fix: Fix IdP condition keys

front: Symptom: Cross-account S3/KMS fail after role fix — what do you check and fix?
back: Check: Resource policy on bucket/key · Fix: Add Principal for role ARN

front: Symptom: InvalidUserID.NotFound — what do you check and fix?
back: Check: Wrong account/ partition in ARN (Amazon Resource Name) · Fix: Fix ARN

front: Symptom: New hire can't console login — what do you check and fix?
back: Check: Identity Center assignment; IdP sync · Fix: Assign permission set; SCIM/group mapping

front: Symptom: AccessDeniedException on PassRole — what do you check and fix?
back: Check: iam:PassRole for deployment roles · Fix: Scope PassRole to specific role ARNs

front: Gotcha with IAM: what silently fails?
back: Default service roles (AWSServiceRoleForSupport, AWSServiceRoleForTrustedAdvisor) — AWS-managed; don't delete; not where your app permissions live.

front: When should you NOT use IAM?
back: IAM users with access keys for application runtime — use instance profile / IRSA / Lambda execution role. Shared root account credentials — enable root MFA; lock root to break-glass only. Duplicating AWS-managed policy by copy-paste — attach AWS managed and add small custom policy for deltas.

front: What is Route53 in one sentence?
back: AWS authoritative DNS + health-checked routing + private zones — not just "create an A record." Route53 Developer Guide + prod cutover war stories.

front: Explain the mental model of Route53 (how the system thinks).
back: Route53 hosts hosted zones (public on the internet, or private associated with VPCs). Records answer queries; routing policies (weighted, latency, failover, geolocation) steer traffic. Health checks remove unhealthy targets from DNS answers (with caveats — DNS TTL caching delays failover).

front: Which standard commands / workflow do you use for Route53?
back: Client resolver ──► Route53 (authoritative for zone) ──► A/AAAA/CNAME/ALIAS → aws route53 list-hosted-zones-by-name --dns-name example.com → aws route53 change-resource-record-sets --hosted-zone-id Z123 --change-batch file://change.json

front: Given a broken Route53 setup, what is your first validation command?
back: Client resolver ──► Route53 (authoritative for zone) ──► A/AAAA/CNAME/ALIAS

front: What are the production-safe defaults for Route53?
back: change.json (ALIAS to ALB):

front: Symptom: Domain doesn't resolve at all — what do you check and fix?
back: Check: NS at registrar match Route53 zone; zone exists · Fix: Update registrar NS; wait propagation (up to 48h, often minutes)

front: Symptom: Resolves old IP after change — what do you check and fix?
back: Check: TTL; cached at resolver/ISP · Fix: Lower TTL pre-change; dig +trace; flush local cache

front: Symptom: Apex works, www doesn't (or reverse) — what do you check and fix?
back: Check: Missing record; CNAME at apex (invalid) · Fix: ALIAS at apex; CNAME for subdomains only

front: Symptom: Private name resolves on laptop, not in VPC — what do you check and fix?
back: Check: PHZ VPC association; enableDnsSupport · Fix: Associate VPC; check hybrid DNS forwarders

front: Symptom: Failover didn't switch — what do you check and fix?
back: Check: Health check region; TTL; EvaluateTargetHealth false · Fix: Fix health check path; enable eval; accept DNS delay

front: Symptom: ACM cert stuck pending validation — what do you check and fix?
back: Check: TXT/CNAME record in same zone ACM expects · Fix: Create exact validation record Route53 can auto-create

front: Symptom: SERVFAIL intermittent — what do you check and fix?
back: Check: Route53 query logging; lame delegations · Fix: Fix child NS; check DS/DNSSEC if enabled

front: Gotcha with Route53: what silently fails?
back: DNS failover is not instant — clients and resolvers cache TTL. Plan for minutes of bleed; use health checks + app-layer retries.

front: When should you NOT use Route53?
back: Sub-millisecond failover requirement — DNS alone insufficient; use anycast LB + health checks at L7/L4. Complex geo compliance — combine with CloudFront/Lambda@Edge; Route53 geolocation is coarse. Full DNS server features (custom AXFR to random NS) — Route53 is managed authoritative, not a general BIND replacement (servers/BIND).

front: What is Security Group in one sentence?
back: Stateful virtual firewall at ENI level — default deny inbound, allow by rule; return traffic automatically permitted. Primary ingress/egress control for EC2, RDS, ELB, Lambda-in-VPC, ElastiCache, etc.

front: What is Least privilege ports?
back: 8080/tcp not -1 (all protocols) unless proven necessary.

front: What is Separate SG per tier?
back: don't reuse default SG.

front: Explain the mental model of Security Group (how the system thinks).
back: A Security Group (SG) is a label + rule set attached to ENIs (instances, load balancers, RDS). Rules are allow-only (no deny rules). Stateful: if inbound TCP 443 is allowed and connection established, return packets flow without explicit outbound rule for that flow.

front: Which standard commands / workflow do you use for Security Group?
back: Internet ──► SG(inbound: 443 from 0.0.0.0/0) ──► EC2:443 → aws ec2 describe-security-groups --group-ids sg-xxx \ → aws ec2 authorize-security-group-ingress \ → aws ec2 create-network-insights-path --source sg-xxx --destination sg-yyy ...

front: Given a broken Security Group setup, what is your first validation command?
back: Internet ──► SG(inbound: 443 from 0.0.0.0/0) ──► EC2:443

front: What are the production-safe defaults for Security Group?
back: Reference SG ids, not CIDR, for east-west traffic — IPs change; SG membership is stable.

front: Symptom: Connection timeout to EC2/RDS — what do you check and fix?
back: Check: SG inbound on destination; outbound on source if non-stateful path · Fix: Add SG-to-SG or CIDR rule on correct port

front: Symptom: Works from one instance, not another — what do you check and fix?
back: Check: Different SG attachment · Fix: Align SG or add missing rule

front: Symptom: ALB targets unhealthy — what do you check and fix?
back: Check: Target SG allows ALB SG on app/health port · Fix: Open port from alb-sg

front: Symptom: Intermittent after scale-out — what do you check and fix?
back: Check: New instances missing SG or wrong SG · Fix: Launch template SG; ASG verify

front: Symptom: "SG looks open" but still blocked — what do you check and fix?
back: Check: NACL; route table; app not listening; wrong VPC · Fix: SG is necessary not sufficient — check full path (AWS Networking)

front: Symptom: IPv6 path broken — what do you check and fix?
back: Check: Separate IPv6 rules in SG (not implied by IPv4) · Fix: Add ::/0 or specific v6 rules explicitly

front: Symptom: Lambda in VPC can't reach RDS — what do you check and fix?
back: Check: Lambda SG + RDS SG reciprocal · Fix: Lambda SG egress + RDS SG inbound from Lambda SG

front: Gotcha with Security Group: what silently fails?
back: Changing SG rules is immediate — no "apply" delay, but existing TCP sessions may not pick up new deny (stateful tracking). Restart connection after rule change.

front: When should you NOT use Security Group?
back: Subnet-wide block list (deny bad IP) — SG has no deny; use NACL or AWS Network Firewall / WAF at edge. Application auth — SG is network layer; never expose admin API to world because "it's password protected." Replacing IAM — opening SG to 0.0.0.0/0 on 443 doesn't replace authn/z at app layer.

front: What is AWS STS (Security Token Service) in one sentence?
back: Short-lived temporary credentials (AccessKeyId, SecretAccessKey, SessionToken) instead of long-lived IAM user keys — foundation for roles, federation, and cross-account access. AWS IAM docs + incident stories from leaked static keys.

front: Explain the mental model of AWS STS (Security Token Service) (how the system thinks).
back: STS is AWS's token mint: you prove identity (IAM user, role, SAML/OIDC, or another account's role), STS returns credentials valid for minutes to hours, bound to an IAM role's permissions. Every AssumeRole, EC2 instance profile, Lambda execution role, and aws sso login session flows through STS.

front: Which standard commands / workflow do you use for AWS STS (Security Token Service)?
back: Caller ──► sts:AssumeRole ──► temporary creds ──► AWS APIs (scoped to role policy) → aws sts get-caller-identity → aws sts assume-role \ → eval "$(aws sts assume-role ... --query 'Credentials.[AccessKeyId,SecretAccessKey,SessionToken]' --output text | \ → awk '{print "export AWS_ACCESS_KEY_ID="$1"\nexport AWS_SECRET_ACCESS_KEY="$2"\nexport AWS_SESSION_TOKEN="$3}')"

front: Given a broken AWS STS (Security Token Service) setup, what is your first validation command?
back: Caller ──► sts:AssumeRole ──► temporary creds ──► AWS APIs (scoped to role policy)

front: What are the production-safe defaults for AWS STS (Security Token Service)?
back: EC2 instance profile → IMDS delivers rotating role creds (prefer IMDSv2: HttpTokens: required). EKS IRSA → OIDC trust to sts:AssumeRoleWithWebIdentity. Lambda → execution role creds injected by runtime.

front: Symptom: AccessDenied on AssumeRole — what do you check and fix?
back: Check: Trust policy Principal; role name/ARN; ExternalId · Fix: Fix trust Principal; pass correct ExternalId

front: Symptom: ExpiredToken mid-deploy — what do you check and fix?
back: Check: Session duration; clock skew on host · Fix: Re-assume; sync NTP; increase duration within max

front: Symptom: Works locally, fails in CI — what do you check and fix?
back: Check: OIDC thumbprint/audience; repo/org condition · Fix: Fix IdP trust; scope sub/aud conditions

front: Symptom: EC2/Lambda "can't reach AWS APIs" — what do you check and fix?
back: Check: Instance profile attached? IMDS blocked? · Fix: Attach profile; fix IMDS hop limit (containers need 2)

front: Symptom: Cross-account S3/KMS denied after assume — what do you check and fix?
back: Check: Resource policy on bucket/key must trust role ARN · Fix: Update bucket/key policy for assumed role principal

front: Symptom: InvalidIdentityToken (EKS) — what do you check and fix?
back: Check: Service account annotation eks.amazonaws.com/role-arn · Fix: IRSA setup; OIDC provider on cluster

front: Gotcha with AWS STS (Security Token Service): what silently fails?
back: Assumed-role creds need all three env vars — AWS_SESSION_TOKEN missing → obscure signature errors.

front: When should you NOT use AWS STS (Security Token Service)?
back: Long-lived IAM user access keys for apps — use roles + STS; keys for break-glass humans only, rotated and scoped. Embedding AssumeRole in every micro-request — cache creds until ~5 min before expiry; use SDK default credential chain. One mega-role for all environments — separate roles per env/account; STS makes splitting cheap.
